hints.title: Grouped Extremum Matching
hints.text: Each department can contain multiple individuals sharing the maximum compensation value. How can employees be filtered by matching both their department association and their compensation against calculated maximums?

hints.title: Composite In-Filter on Aggregates
hints.text: Grouping records by department determines the peak compensation for each unit. Filtering the base table using a composite tuple match on department identifier and compensation keeps all top earners.

hints.title: Group Subquery with Department Join
hints.text: Compute the maximum salary per department using a grouped subquery on departmentId. Join Employee with Department, and filter records where the tuple of departmentId and salary matches the subquery results. Select the department name, employee name, and salary.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT d.name AS Department, e.name AS Employee, e.salary AS Salary
FROM Employee e
JOIN Department d ON e.departmentId = d.id
WHERE (e.departmentId, e.salary) IN (
  SELECT departmentId, MAX(salary)
  FROM Employee
  GROUP BY departmentId
);
```

complexity.notes: Inner join with grouped maximum salary subquery on (departmentId, salary).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries in the SELECT clause (SELECT (SELECT MAX(...) ... WHERE ...)) execute once per employee row (O(E * E) full scans). Joining without a composite tuple match (departmentId, salary) can mismatch salaries across different departments.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Grouping once by department to compute MAX(salary) requires O(E) time and O(D) hash table memory, enabling an optimal hash-semijoin in O(E + D) total execution time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling salary ties properly (if two employees in the same department share the max salary, both must be returned); using composite tuple matching or window functions (DENSE_RANK()).

solutions.code:
SELECT d.name AS Department, e.name AS Employee, e.salary AS Salary
FROM Employee e
JOIN Department d ON e.departmentId = d.id
WHERE (e.departmentId, e.salary) IN (
  SELECT departmentId, MAX(salary)
  FROM Employee
  GROUP BY departmentId
);

SELECT d.name AS "Department", e.name AS "Employee", e.salary AS "Salary"
FROM Employee e
JOIN Department d ON e.departmentId = d.id
WHERE (e.departmentId, e.salary) IN (
  SELECT departmentId, MAX(salary)
  FROM Employee
  GROUP BY departmentId
);
